summary: Respond.io paginates every list endpoint with an integer cursorId (pagination.next as a JSON number), not the string 'after' the generator defaulted to. Recognize numeric next cursors, send cursorId on sync for contact/message/space, and wire `contact list --all` to loop pages by threading pagination.next back into the body's cursorId.
reason: The Respond.io API silently ignores a cursor parameter named 'after' and returns the cursor as a JSON number inside pagination.next, which the generated extractor (string-only cursorKeys without 'next') could never read. Contact sync therefore stopped after one page without even emitting the pagination_cursor_missing warning, and `contact list --all` was a no-op that silently returned one page. The generic generator encodes a string cursor named 'after'; the durable fix is a generator/template improvement for numeric cursorId APIs, hardened here for the shipped binary.
